selected.title: He Secretly Swapped My Engagement Ring
selected.hook: The jeweler told me my engagement ring had been returned six months ago. It was still on my finger.
selected.voiceover:
The jeweler told me my engagement ring had been returned six months ago. It was still on my finger.

My fiance proposed last winter with a ring we had looked at together before. I knew the design, the store, even a tiny scratch near the setting.

Last week, I went back because one of the stones felt loose.

The employee pulled up the purchase and looked confused.

Then she said, "This ring was returned in March."

March was two weeks after he proposed.

I thought there had to be another order.

There wasn't.

At home, I compared photos from the proposal with the ring I was wearing. Same design, but the tiny scratch was gone.

My fiance finally admitted he had returned the original and bought a cheaper replica online.

He needed the refund to cover credit-card debt he had never told me about.

He said the replacement looked identical, I was happy, and the "meaning" of the ring hadn't changed.

But he had watched me show it to my parents, insure it, and talk about passing it down someday, knowing it wasn't the ring he proposed with.

Now he says I'm focusing on the price instead of our engagement.

I don't care that the replacement was cheaper.

I care that he secretly rewrote the story attached to it.

Would you still wear the ring after learning your fiance swapped it without telling you?
selected.youtube_description:
She took her engagement ring back to the jeweler for a loose stone and learned the original ring had been returned just two weeks after the proposal. What looked like a simple repair uncovered hidden debt and a secret swap she never agreed to. Does the value of an engagement ring come from the price, or from the honesty behind it?
